title: Joining Buddy Petit's band
summary: Allen opens the interview asking about Over the Lake with Buddy Petit. Zardis names the six-piece band (Washington, Faiso, Edmund Hall, Manaday on banjo) and says Marrero introduced him to Buddy.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: This is February the 14th, 1970. Yes, Ray. And we're interviewing Tester Zardes, and we're in Preservation Hall. Yes, Ray. All right, Tester, well, one of the main things I wanted to ask you about was when you were playing in Over the Lake, in the early 20s or whenever it was, with Buddy Petit. Yeah, 19, 20, that's right. Okay, well, now, can you tell me everything you can remember about that, how you met Buddy and what way you would play and who else was in the band and generally all kinds of things like that. I mean, I'm really interested in Buddy Petit himself.

Well, you see, the way we started off, I was playing with a band out of, you know, around here in town until I got professional. I didn't get professional until I got with Buddy's band, you know what I mean? And Buddy had a pretty nice band. It was George Washington on trombone, and he had Faiso on drums. Then you had Edmund Hall on clarinet, and Buddy Petit was playing the trumpet. See? We didn't have, but there were six pieces, you know? Yeah. You know? And this boy, Hall, Hall was a pretty nice, you know, nice musician. I wish Buddy had really one of the best bands, you know? And after I got with Buddy, well then I commenced, you know, getting professional, real professional. See? Because after I got to be knowing, and I knew what I was doing, see? Because I was around here playing with these bands, and I didn't, wasn't playing like I should play. Well, Buddy Manatee, he was the banjo player with Buddy Petit's band.
And he showed me a whole lot, and from that on, well, I just went until I left Buddy. Well, I stayed with Buddy a long time.
How did you meet him? Can you remember?

Yeah, well, Buddy, he was raised up down my way, see, in the Seven Ward day. He was raised up, and after I heard that he had a band, so he came over and see me. Buddy, I mean, this Billy Marrera, that's my teacher, and he told Buddy about me. And that's where Buddy asked me would I join these bands, so I told him, yeah, I joined these bands, which I did. And before we left here and went to Covington, we was working at the St. Bernard Market, was playing there every Saturday evening, see? Around, say, about seven o'clock until nine o'clock, you know?
